question.text: The line <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> form an isosceles triangle with the planes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, then the value of <math><mi>k</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
If given line makes an isosceles triangle with the planes, then the angle that the line makes with the normal vectors to the planes are equal
A vector parallel to the line is b→=<k,2,-12>
A normal vector to the first plane n1→=<2,1,3>
A normal vector to the second plane n2→=<1,2,-3>
cosθ= b → ⋅ n i → b → n 1 → = b → ⋅ n 2 → b → n 2 → ⇒2k+2−36=k+4+36
⇒k=74
